summary: You demonstrated solid architectural reasoning, clear structure, and strong trade-off analysis in your modular monolith evaluation. However, marks were dropped due to vague response metrics in Q1, an incomplete series calculation in Q3(c), inverted Circuit Breaker states in Q4, a CAP theorem misconception in Q5, one-sided ADR consequences in Q6, and a missing reference citation.
next_steps: Ensure all quality attribute response measures are quantified using precise metrics (e.g., uptime percentages or MTTR) rather than subjective phrasing.
Correct technical definitions: in Circuit Breaker, traffic flows during Closed states, and network partitions (P) in distributed systems cannot be opted out of under CAP.
When documenting architecture decisions, explicitly identify negative consequences, operational overheads, or trade-offs alongside the benefits.

criteria.C1: You selected and justified relevant quality attributes well. To reach Excellent, ensure both response measures are strictly measurable; replace vague phrases like 'stay up most of the time' with concrete metrics such as 99.9% uptime or MTTR under 5 minutes.
criteria.C2: Excellent work. You provided a clear, scenario-specific recommendation for a modular monolith, effectively balancing team size, scaling, and rolling deployments while explicitly acknowledging process-level crash risks and independent scaling downsides.
criteria.C3: Parts (a) and (b) were executed correctly. To achieve Excellent, carry through the full composite calculation in part (c) by multiplying your parallel payment availability (99.9975%) back into the remaining series components.
criteria.C4: You correctly identified the Circuit Breaker pattern. To reach Excellent, accurately describe its mechanism (Closed allows traffic, Open fails fast), and include tuning considerations (e.g., reset timeouts) or drawbacks.
criteria.C5: Menu browsing consistency was handled well. For Excellent, apply CAP correctly—distributed systems cannot forfeit partition tolerance (P)—and supply a concrete technique for the payment case (such as distributed transactions or the Saga pattern).
criteria.C6: Context and Decision sections were well-tailored to the scenario. To achieve Excellent, balance the Consequences section by including at least one negative trade-off, operational downside, or added complexity alongside the benefits.
criteria.C7: Your writing was clear, concise, and followed structural constraints. To achieve Excellent, verify that every in-text citation (such as [2] in Question 4) has a corresponding entry in the reference list.
